clue.text: Stand or fall with party backing

parts.note: to trip is to fall over

indicators.note: backing means the word for a party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political choice: support or go down with the party behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns DO into OD. 'Stand or fall' reads as the stock phrase, but 'Stand' alone is the definition and 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera is a stand of this kind.

clue.text: Insure a possible harvest

annotationWithheld.why: 'Insure a possible harvest': the answer is hidden in 'insuRE A Possible', and the only hiding signal is the 'In' at the start of 'Insure', so that word is both indicator and fodder

clue.text: Promote president to pram

parts.note: to push a product is to promote it
a chair presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: Elevating the president to a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pram and a folding baby buggy are both wheeled carriers for infants.

clue.text: Settle government department's year

parts.note: DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

explanation.surface: Fixing a ministry's annual budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle costs is to pay them, the sense of covering expenses.

clue.text: Near expert in native American detail

indicators.note: in places the expert inside the curtailed tribe's name
de-tail means the last letter, the tail, is cut off

parts.note: the Apache are a native American people
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: Seemingly about an expert closely studying Native American matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like 'particulars' but splits as de-tail, removing the last letter, the tail, of the tribe's name.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to near something is to come closer to it.

clue.text: You'll hardly find whips as tolerant as this

definitions.text: You'll hardly find whips as tolerant as this

indicators.note: hardly suggests the words are barely themselves, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Party disciplinarians are rarely so lenient.
explanation.walkthrough: Whips, the officials who enforce party voting discipline, are rarely this lenient; and the anagram of WHIPS AS TOLERANT, signalled by 'hardly', gives the mild punishment itself, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A token light punishment is idiomatically a small smack on the hand rather than real chastisement.

clue.text: Make holes in (not at) round number necessarily

indicators.note: in puts the round number inside the shortened verb
not at means those two letters are removed

parts.note: to perforate is to make holes
taken as written
C, the Roman hundred, is a round number

explanation.surface: Instructions to punch holes, with a parenthetical aside, around a figure, of necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not at)' removes those two letters from the verb; 'in' then puts the Roman hundred, a round number, inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means by force of circumstance, hence unavoidably or of necessity.

clue.text: Refreshing spot of love for a relation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
sis, short for sister, is a relation

explanation.surface: A place to relax where one finds romance for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert oasis is a fertile watered spot offering refreshment.

clue.text: Shout about gold turning into a warning

indicators.note: about means the shout goes round the rest

parts.note: to cry is to shout
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of into a are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yells as gold transforms into a cautionary sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges INTO A into TIONA, and 'about' wraps the shout round gold plus those letters. 'warning' is used adjectivally, as in a warning tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in a warning tale, it means serving to caution.

clue.text: Zoroastrian flower in opera

parts.note: a Parsi is a follower of Zoroastrianism in India
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A Persian bloom appears in a stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (it flows); the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's last music drama, about the Grail knight, is a well-known opera.

clue.text: Occasion for engineers to talk of salvation

indicators.note: for reverses the clue order: an occasion for engineers is the engineers' cue

parts.note: the REs are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a cue is the signal or occasion to act

explanation.surface: Engineers being given a chance to speak about being saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion for engineers' is the REs' cue, read in that order; 'to talk of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being saved from danger is both salvation and being delivered to safety.

clue.text: The second division of advocacy

definitions.meaning: in English football the second tier, below the Premier League, is so named
championing a cause means speaking up for it, the act of advocacy

explanation.surface: Football's second tier seems to be a branch of legal pleading.
explanation.walkthrough: The Championship is the English football league just below the Premier League, in old terms the Second Division.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocacy of a cause is support for it; the second tier of English football carries this name.

clue.text: Teacher measures hill after short climb

indicators.note: after places the hill at the end

parts.note: ins are inches, measures of length

indicators.note: climb in a down clue means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: curt means short
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: An instructor gauges a hill after a brief ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climb' reads a word upwards, so 'short' reversed gives TRUC; 'after' puts the hill last.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who instructs, such as a driving or ski coach, is a teacher.

clue.text: Girl no longer current

definitions.meaning: an old Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee, no longer legal currency

explanation.surface: A young woman is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' puns on currency: the anna was an Indian coin withdrawn in 1957.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female name, and a former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: One home in nine has lethal possibilities

definitions.note: describes a substance that can kill, standing for its name

indicators.note: in puts one and a home inside the number

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
a cot is a small cottage, a home

explanation.surface: Statistics: one household in nine is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: the clue says what the substance can do, a typical Araucaria looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: The alkaloid in tobacco is a potent poison, deadly in concentrated doses.

clue.text: Poster etc can be very hush-hush

indicators.note: can be signals the letters may be made into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Posters and the like can be highly confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges the letters of POSTER ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified material at the highest level is extremely confidential, which is what hush-hush means.

clue.text: Bramley in America?

parts.note: a Bramley is a large British cooking fruit; seen in the US, it suggests New York's nickname

explanation.surface: A British cooking fruit transplanted to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bramley is a large British cooking apple; the question mark flags that New York's nickname is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bramley is a big cooking fruit, and the American city nickname fits literally.

clue.text: Marine invertebrate put right back if put away outside

indicators.note: outside means the hoarding word wraps round the rest

parts.note: to stash is to put away

indicators.note: back means the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to return a sea creature, tucking it away if possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the little word if, and 'outside' has the hoarding word wrap round right plus those letters; 'put' before 'right' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-armed echinoderm is a marine creature without a backbone.

clue.text: Reduce sound of 2 from 2

indicators.note: sound of says the word is heard, spelled differently

parts.note: two things make a pair

explanation.surface: A numerical riddle about trimming one number from another.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is a pair, which 'sound of' turns into a homophone; 'from 2' also points at 2-down, REAP, whose letters rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare costs is to cut them back, trim or diminish.

clue.text: American fuel source with which one could do

indicators.note: source here suggests the letters are worked into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A US energy supply that would come in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' is an unusual anagram signal, rearranging FUEL into EFUL; 'with which one could do' means handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one could do with is handy, of practical value.

clue.text: Problem in keeping menu clear was testing

indicators.note: keeping means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Trouble keeping a restaurant's menu clear was a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'meNU CLEAR WAS TEsting'; 'keeping' signals the hiding and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent radioactive material is a notorious environmental problem.

clue.text: Prone to terminological inexactitude

explanation.surface: Inclined to use misleading terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill coined 'terminological inexactitude' in 1906 as a polite word for untruth; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prone means flat, horizontal; the euphemism means telling untruths, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Conveyance for one within the pale?

indicators.note: within places one inside the pale

parts.note: wan means pale
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vehicle for someone inside the safe boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within the pale' suggests the old English boundary round Dublin, but pale here means WAN, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is an old farm wagon, a means of transporting goods.

clue.text: Possibly the first work of the man from Addis

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the could be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, so first
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Possibly the debut work of a man from Ethiopia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges THE into ETH; Addis Ababa is Ethiopia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic word for an Ethiopian, someone from Addis Ababa's country.

clue.text: Broke nail grasping plant from hell

indicators.note: grasping means the shattered letters hold the plant
broke signals the letters of nail are broken up

parts.note: taken as written
a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A snapped fingernail catching on some greenery from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' rearranges NAIL into INAL, and 'grasping' has those letters hold the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal describes things belonging to the underworld, as hellish does.

clue.text: Bit journalists in foot?

indicators.note: in places journalists inside the abbreviation for foot

parts.note: rag men: a rag is a tabloid newspaper, so its staff are rag men

explanation.surface: Reporters underfoot?
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is slang for a cheap newspaper, so the men who write for one are journalists; the question mark flags the odd image.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken piece, a bit.

clue.text: Set off any questions?

parts.note: to light a fuse is to set it off; lit is its past form

explanation.surface: Triggering any queries at all?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a litany is a long series of petitions or questions, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a repetitive series of petitions, by extension a long list of queries or complaints.
